newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krenz fails in bid to prove German court is biased.
newsitem.headline: Krenz fails in bid to prove German court is biased.

text.p: East Germany's last hardline communist leader, Egon Krenz, failed on Monday in a bid to have the judges trying him on manslaughter charges dismissed because they refused to call Chancellor Helmut Kohl as a witness.
Krenz's lawyer lodged an objection claiming the judges' refusal to call Kohl showed they were biased.
Krenz alleges that Kohl and then-Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev agreed in 1990 that no East German leaders would be prosecuted if they had not broken the law of their own country.

He and three other top officials have been on trial since November last year, charged with repsonsibilty for the deaths of East German citizens trying to flee over the Berlin Wall or across the fortifified border which ran the length of the two Germanys.
Presiding judge Josef Hoch said Krenz's application had nothing to do with the trial and was simply a stunt to try to force the court to call Kohl as a witness.
The court had rejected Krenz's application to call Kohl last week, saying any agreement between the chancellor and Gorbachev was not relevant to the trial.
